answer: Shards are assigned from the canyon graph, which means cluster membership directly reduces grading power. The karst assignment is published and velvet records each panel. The grading quorum of 4 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so a hostile operator cannot sit on the panel that judges it. A farm of 3273 identities would post 1700 proofs and burn roughly 86 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
